definition: The Barzilai–Borwein method is an iterative gradient descent method for unconstrained optimization using either of two step sizes derived from the linear trend of the most recent two iterates.
details: This method, and modifications, are globally convergent under mild conditions, and perform competitively with conjugate gradient methods for many problems. Not depending on the objective itself, it can also solve some systems of linear and non-linear equations.
story: Imagine teaching a friend to shoot a basketball. They miss, and you walk them backwards through the shot — elbow, wrist, release — to find what needs fixing. Boil it down and it is this: The Barzilai–Borwein method is an iterative gradient descent method for unconstrained optimization using either of two step sizes derived from the linear trend of the most recent two iterates. Here is why it matters: This method, and modifications, are globally convergent under mild conditions, and perform competitively with conjugate gradient methods for many problems. It is learning from every miss instead of repeating the same mistake. That steady, miss-by-miss improvement is Barzilai–Borwein method.
